title: Tiny Graph First Path
public_summary: Learn GraphReFly as a declared topology first: inputs enter the graph, derived nodes reduce them, and effects observe the result at the boundary.

public_sections.heading: 1. Declare Inputs
body: Start by naming the facts that can change. In package code these may be state nodes, sources, or package-local helpers, but the shared mental model is simply explicit inputs.
bullets: Use real domain facts, not placeholder lifecycle values.
Keep external IO at source or adapter boundaries.
Pick the language package only when you need runnable syntax.

public_sections.heading: 2. Derive a Reduced Value
body: A derived node turns one or more inputs into a smaller value. The graph owns the dependency shape, so joins and updates stay explainable.
bullets: Declare dependencies instead of manually triggering downstream work.
Let the wave protocol coordinate fan-in.
Keep reductions pure unless the package helper explicitly models an effect boundary.

public_sections.heading: 3. Observe at the Edge
body: Effects are where the outside world reacts. The shared docs stop at the composition shape; concrete effect APIs, examples, demos, and install commands live with each package.
bullets: Use TypeScript, Python, or Rust docs for runnable code.
Use composition records for cross-language patterns.
Use examples records for recipe intent and package links.
